To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the LPa3 neuron of the left paraventricular ganglion of Lymnaea stagnalis is a polyfunctional neuron that has a receptive field with three zones.

(1) the receptive field of LPa3 neuron is a complex structure, consisting of three areas, each of which is linked to LPa3 neuron by its own parallel channel; (2) the right pallial nerve is responsible for the transmission of the short latency rapidly-extinguishing component of the response to the mantle, the anal nerve transmits the slowly extinguishing long-latency component, and the left pallial transmits a slowly-extinguishing multi-component response;

the LPa3 neuron of the snail has a receptive field consisting of the three zones: right, left, and pneumostome, each of which is innervated through different channels, the pallial and anal, and the left pallial nerves, respectively.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the receptive field plasticity in the LPa3 neuron of the left parieal ganglion of Helisoma trivolvis snail.
the plastic properties of the receptive fields in a polyfunctional neurone of the mollusc central nervous system.
the study of the plastic properties of the receptive fields of identified neurones of the CNS in mollusks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the receptive fields of the LPa 3 neurone are composed of a number of zones, each of which is innervated via a specific channel, and the properties of which are different.
in the LPa3 neuron the receptive field is a system of parallel pathways with different properties.
the LPa3 neuron has a very complicated receptive field and that its plastic properties are not uniform throughout this field.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the plasticity of the receptive field depends on the number and functional characteristics of the parallel channels linking the neuron with the effector organ.
the LPa3 neuron is capable of receiving and transmitting different types of information, and the plasticity of its receptive field is due to the different properties of the parallel pathways.
in molluscs the synaptic transmission is not only a mechanism for the transfer of information, but also for the formation of a new information.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the receptive field of an LPa3 neurones is not a simple summation of the receptive fields of the nerves which innervate the neurone, but is a complex system of parallel channels with a specific structure.
the LPa3 neuron has a complex receptive field, and its response is determined by the activity of a number of parallel synaptic channels.
a polyfunctional neurone can be involved in the formation of the receptive field with a complex structure.
